title: Petra and the Colony
premise: On the isolated colony of Vesper's Landing, Astrid Nystrom keeps a beacon no one will claim, until the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream: a night of fire in the old habitat, and a door that must not open. When the children start vanishing into the dream itself, Astrid discovers the beacon is a lock — and that the colony's founding families rewrote every record to bury a massacre aboard the first ship. To save the children, Astrid must reopen the sealed archive her own grandmother helped falsify, choosing truth over the loyalty that built her family's name, even as the colony's rulers move to purge the evidence and the witnesses. In the end Astrid opens the door, releases the trapped memory of the murdered colonists, and shatters the founders' power — but the children who crossed over return changed, carrying names of the dead that no living person ever knew.
about_author: Tamsin Sandoval is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction about records that lie. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the northern coast, where she maintains, on principle, a light nobody asked her to keep.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Astrid Nystrom makes her monthly climb to maintain an unregistered beacon whose maintenance contract predates all colony records. Her POV establishes her meticulous loneliness and the odd clause in her employment: 'until it is needed.' Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Shared Weather
chapters.summary: Schoolteacher Dev Okafor notices thirty-one children drawing identical images: a burning corridor and a numbered door. Dev's POV; he dismisses it as a game until two children describe details of the original ship's layout that were demolished decades ago. Beat: creeping dread.

chapters.title: Clause Seven
chapters.summary: Astrid audits her own contract and finds Clause Seven, activating if 'the dream recurs.' She doesn't know what dream means. Meanwhile Councilor Maren Hale requests a friendly meeting. Astrid's POV. Beat: the sense of being watched by paperwork.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Slept Too Long
chapters.summary: Nine-year-old Ilsa Voss won't wake. Her parents refuse hospital transfer, whispering that waking her 'breaks the count.' Dev's POV as he witnesses the family's fear and the council's smooth interference. Beat: helplessness curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Tea with Maren Hale
chapters.summary: Maren offers Astrid a generous early retirement and hints the beacon is 'legacy infrastructure, best forgotten.' Astrid notes Maren's hands shaking. Astrid's POV. Beat: politeness as a weapon; first taste of institutional menace.

chapters.title: What the Children Say
chapters.summary: Dev secretly records the dreaming children talking in their sleep — they speak in unison, using archaic ship jargon and one repeated phrase: 'the door remembers us.' Dev's POV. Beat: awe tipping into terror.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Box
chapters.summary: Astrid finds her late grandmother's locked tin: a maintenance log for the beacon dated before the colony's official founding, and a photograph of crew members whose faces are scratched out. Astrid's POV. Beat: inheritance revealed as burden.

chapters.title: The Founders' Version
chapters.summary: In the colony archive, Astrid reads the official history: the seed ship Meridian arrived intact, no casualties, glorious founding. The dates don't fit the beacon log. Astrid's POV. Beat: the first hard proof that records lie.

chapters.title: Second Sleeper
chapters.summary: Ilsa wakes — but speaks only in another woman's voice, asking for someone named Ede. The Vosses beg Dev to tell no one. Dev's POV. Beat: grief wearing a child's face.

chapters.title: Hale's Warning
chapters.summary: Maren escalates: a formal inquiry into Astrid's 'unauthorized archival access.' Astrid realizes the council monitors everything. She hides Grandmother's tin inside the beacon housing. Astrid's POV. Beat: paranoia becomes survival skill.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Dev tallies the dreamers: forty children began; nine have slept. He maps sleepers against founding-family surnames — all nine descend from Meridian crew. Dev's POV. Beat: pattern recognition as horror.

chapters.title: Ede
chapters.summary: Astrid decodes her grandmother's marginalia: Ede was her grandmother's sister, listed as lost with eleven others in an 'airlock malfunction' that appears nowhere else. Astrid's POV. Beat: personal grief fusing with public crime.

chapters.title: Blackout Night
chapters.summary: The colony grid fails for exactly seven minutes — the same duration as the dream's fire. Every sleeper sits upright simultaneously. Dev witnesses it at the clinic. Dev's POV. Beat: the past asserting itself in the present.

chapters.title: The Old Habitat
chapters.summary: Astrid explores the derelict first habitat and finds a wall of scratched tally marks — forty-one — behind a panel stamped with the beacon's serial number. Astrid's POV. Beat: physical evidence the archive denies.

chapters.title: Loyalty Lessons
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Astrid learning from her grandmother that 'we keep what we're given and ask nothing.' Now Astrid understands what was given and why silence was the price. Astrid's POV. Beat: love and complicity entangled.

chapters.title: Council Session
chapters.summary: Maren convenes an emergency session Astrid crashes via an old maintenance channel. She hears them vote to decommission the beacon — which she now knows would seal the door permanently, with the children inside whatever waits. Astrid's POV. Beat: stakes made explicit.

chapters.title: Alliance
chapters.summary: Astrid and Dev compare notes for the first time, trading the tin, the recordings, and the tally marks. Neither trusts easily; both decide to. Dev's POV. Beat: wary partnership kindled.

chapters.title: Inside the Dream
chapters.summary: Astrid deliberately sleeps at the beacon during its activation window. She dreams the corridor: fire, screaming, a hand on the door handle from the other side — Ede's hand. Astrid's POV. Beat: witness turned participant.

chapters.title: What Really Happened
chapters.summary: The dream shows the truth: when the Meridian's life support failed, forty-one crew drew lots to stay behind so the rest could launch. The survivors — the founders — then erased them to found a colony without debt. Astrid's POV. Beat: massacre confirmed; motive understood.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Name
chapters.summary: Dev cross-references the dream-names against genetic registries: the sleeping children aren't random — they're descendants of the forty-one, called home. His own daughter is on the list. Dev's POV. Beat: abstract cause turns intimate.

chapters.title: Retraction
chapters.summary: Maren publicly accuses Astrid of fabricating evidence and endangering children. The colony turns; Dev's clinic access revoked. Astrid's POV. Beat: isolation, the cost of going public.

chapters.title: The Tin Confiscated
chapters.summary: Council agents seize Grandmother's tin from the beacon — but Astrid has already copied everything onto the beacon's own core, hidden in the maintenance signal she broadcasts nightly. Astrid's POV. Beat: small victory inside defeat.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered by Astrid's evidence, Maren admits her ancestor led the cover-up — and reveals the beacon was built by the guilty as penance, its 'keeper' clause a trap they hoped would never spring. Maren's POV. Beat: villain humanized; corruption shown as inherited cowardice.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: The council votes to destroy the beacon in six days. Astrid has until then to bring the children back or they'll be inside when it burns. Astrid's POV. Beat: clock starts.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Awake
chapters.summary: Astrid and Dev risk everything telling the truth to the sleeper families. Some slam doors; the Vosses join them. Dev's POV. Beat: courage contagious, resistance organized.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone cuts the beacon's power. Astrid climbs in a storm to restore it manually and nearly dies, saved by Ilsa's mother. Astrid's POV. Beat: the keeper's vow tested in blood.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Following the beacon's serial number, they find a sublevel under the old habitat: the founders' true vault, holding the original Meridian logs and forty-one recorded final messages. Dev's POV. Beat: the dead given back their voices.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: They play the final messages colony-wide through the emergency system. The founding myth cracks in real time; half the colony stands with them by morning. Dev's POV. Beat: truth as avalanche.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren must vote on her own order. She recants, exposing the council's plan to burn the vault too, and is arrested by her own security chief. Maren's POV. Beat: redemption purchased at ruin.

chapters.title: Last Sleepers
chapters.summary: Three children remain under, including Ilsa — the dream won't release them until someone answers the door from outside. Astrid understands: it needs the keeper. Astrid's POV. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Astrid spends the evening writing letters she may not send, rereading her grandmother's last entry: 'If you read this, forgive me, and finish it.' Astrid's POV. Beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Opening the Door
chapters.summary: At the beacon, Astrid reverses the lock and steps into the dream's corridor, facing the fire and the forty-one. She speaks the names from the vault, giving the dead their witness. Astrid's POV. Beat: climax begins.

chapters.title: The Corridor
chapters.summary: Inside, Astrid meets Ede, who asks not for rescue but for remembrance — to be carried out as truth, not ghost. Astrid agrees to carry the record, not replace the dead. Astrid's POV. Beat: the theme resolved in dialogue with the past.

chapters.title: Counting Back
chapters.summary: The children wake one by one as each name is spoken aloud in the waking world, Dev reading from the vault logs. Ilsa wakes last, saying only 'thank you' in her own voice. Dev's POV. Beat: release, interwoven with Astrid still missing.

chapters.title: The Empty Climb
chapters.summary: Dawn: the beacon stands dark. Searchers find Astrid asleep at its base, alive, aged somehow, unable to recall the walk down. Astrid's POV. Beat: survival with a scar; mystery honored.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: The colony convenes a truth tribunal. Records are rewritten openly this time; the forty-one are inscribed on the founding monument beside the founders. Dev testifies with his daughter watching. Dev's POV. Beat: justice as process, not spectacle.

chapters.title: What the Children Kept
chapters.summary: The returned children remember pieces of the dead — skills, songs, a recipe, Ede's laugh. The colony debates whether this is gift or wound, and chooses to keep it. Dev's POV. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Maren's Penance
chapters.summary: Maren, stripped of office, takes over the beacon's maintenance rota alongside Astrid — the guilty line finally serving the memory instead of erasing it. Maren's POV. Beat: corruption answered with service.

chapters.title: New Contract
chapters.summary: Astrid drafts a new beacon charter in plain language: kept by choice, witnessed by all, no clauses in the dark. She signs it first, then passes the pen. Astrid's POV. Beat: power rebuilt transparently.

chapters.title: The Light Still Burns
chapters.summary: One year later, the colony gathers at the beacon on Remembrance Night. Forty-one names, forty-one children lighting lamps. Astrid climbs alone one last time and finds the next keeper already waiting — a child who dreams, gently, of an open door. Astrid's POV. Beat: inheritance transformed; ending on continuity and peace.
